economy.essentials_note: Abstracts routine clothing, fuel, soap, basic household goods and other recurring necessities. These are not player-facing purchases.

storylets.title: The Factory Recruiter
storylets.text: A textile mill recruiter visits the neighborhood seeking young hands. With household finances strained, your parents consider sending you to the mill.

choices.label: Accept your parents' decision and enter the mill
choices.description: Leave school to earn wages as a child factory worker.

choices.label: Plead to remain in school and continue your studies
choices.description: Your guardian may listen if they value learning or if your will is strong.

choices.label: Offer to run evening errands without quitting school
choices.description: Exhausting, but helps the household while keeping you in class.

storylets.title: Reading by Candlelight
storylets.text: You have obtained a battered booklet of history and practical arithmetic. After a full day's toll, you have a quiet hour before sleep.

choices.label: Read and copy passages by candlelight
choices.description: Advances literacy significantly at the cost of sleep and eye fatigue.

choices.label: Blow out the candle and rest your weary body
choices.description: Health comes first; tomorrow requires strength.

storylets.title: A Heavy Night Shift
storylets.text: The overseer announces rush orders for export cloth. Anyone staying through the night will receive bonus wages, but machinery speeds are raised.

choices.label: Take the extra shift for hard coin
choices.description: Brings in immediate emergency money, but risks fatigue and injury.

choices.label: Clock out with your regular shift
choices.description: Return to your family in one piece.

storylets.title: The Pawnbroker's Counter
storylets.text: With debts mounting, the pawnbroker's shop offers immediate relief in exchange for the family's last silver timepiece.

choices.label: Pawn the timepiece for ready money
choices.description: Provides needed cash buffer but brings grief and lower willpower.

choices.label: Refuse to part with family memory
choices.description: Your pride stands firm, but hunger will test your resolve.

storylets.title: The Charitable Dispensary
storylets.text: A physician volunteer operates a small dispensary for poor parishioners. Medicine is dispensed to those who wait in line.

choices.label: Wait patiently for examination and tonics
choices.description: Spend a meager coin on apothecary fees to accelerate recovery.

choices.label: Stay home and trust in constitutional strength
choices.description: Save money and avoid contagion from other sick patients.

storylets.title: The Friendly Society
storylets.text: Brothers of the local working-class lodge invite you to join their mutual benefit society, pooling sick funds and burial insurance.

choices.label: Pay the dues and enter the society
choices.description: Invest in communal protection against future ruin.

choices.label: Politely decline and keep every penny
choices.description: Trust only your own savings ledger.

storylets.title: A Walk by the Irwell
storylets.text: After months of shared walks after chapel and careful courtesies, your partner speaks openly of taking wedding vows and sharing a hearth together.

choices.label: Take wedding vows and unite your households
choices.description: Your spouse enters the household. Two incomes strengthen the home, but family obligations begin.

choices.label: Postpone wedding plans until finances are firmer
choices.description: Avoid the costs and responsibilities of married life for now.

storylets.title: The Blacksmith's Bellows
storylets.text: A master smith at the end of the alley needs a sharp lad to pump the heavy bellows and sweep hot cinders. It pays a few pennies and teaches the smell of iron.

choices.label: Take the hammer and learn the trade
choices.description: Earn small wages and learn practical grit, though soot stings your lungs.

choices.label: Remain in the alley with your friends
choices.description: Treasure what little childhood remains before factory years.

storylets.title: Foul Water at the Pump
storylets.text: The public water pump smells of canal runoff, and two neighbors have perished of sudden cramps and fever. Doctors warn that cholera walks the streets of Manchester.

choices.label: Spend scarce pennies on coal to boil every drop
choices.description: Costly fuel shields your family from the pestilence.

choices.label: Rely on the local pump and pray for strength
choices.description: Saves money, but the dirty pump tests your constitution.

storylets.title: The Cotton Panic
storylets.text: War in America has choked off Southern cotton ships. The mills stand silent, boilers cold. Foremen announce half-time wages and mass dismissals across Lancashire.

choices.label: Swallow your pride and seek soup kitchen relief
choices.description: Public charity feeds the household through the bitter winter.

choices.label: Scramble for heavy canal haulage odd jobs
choices.description: Brutal back-breaking labor that keeps you independent of relief.

storylets.title: The Landlord's Knock
storylets.text: A stern agent from the landlord company delivers notice: tenement rents are climbing. Families who cannot pay by month's end will have their mattresses put on the cobbles.

choices.label: Pinch every farthing and meet the landlord's demand
choices.description: Keeps your roof safe at the cost of empty pantry shelves.

choices.label: Organize neighbors to petition against the extortion
choices.description: Collective defiance gains respect, but risks prompt bailiff visits.

storylets.title: The Temperance Banner
storylets.text: Workers flock to the noisy tavern after grueling shifts, while chapel reformers hold torchlit rallies outside, urging men and women to sign the pledge of total abstinence.

choices.label: Take the ribbon and sign the sobriety pledge
choices.description: Protects your health and purse, gaining parish esteem.

choices.label: Join your workmates by the tavern hearth
choices.description: Warm fellowship washes away the week's soot, at modest expense.

storylets.title: A Match for Your Child
storylets.text: Your grown child has found a companion from a respected tradesman family. A wedding banquet and humble trousseau will launch them on their own path.

choices.label: Bless the match and endow their new household
choices.description: Provides gifts and bedding, deepening family honor and joy.

choices.label: Counsel a simple chapel signing without fanfare
choices.description: Preserves savings for your own old age, though spirits dampen.

storylets.title: The Crown Inspector
storylets.text: A Crown factory inspector visits your workplace to investigate unguarded gears and excessive youth hours. The overseer glares at the shop floor with silent warnings.

choices.label: Testify honestly about the perilous machinery
choices.description: Courageous truth-telling secures safety reforms and self-respect.

choices.label: Keep silent and focus on your spindle
choices.description: Protects your steady position without risking the overseer's wrath.

storylets.title: The Heavy Loom
storylets.text: Your hands tremble at the shuttle and your knees ache in the damp air. The family urges you to leave the factory dust to the younger generation.

choices.label: Step down from the loom and rest by the hearth
choices.description: Retire from paid labor; health and peace of mind mend in gentle years.

choices.label: Cling to your station as long as breath permits
choices.description: You earn your keep until the end, refusing to be a burden on anyone.

storylets.title: Cradle and the Loom
storylets.text: Your mother must return to the cotton mill to keep the family fed. The neighbor offers to mind you for a few pence, though infant sleeping draughts are whispered in the alleys.

choices.label: Leave the infant in the dame minder's crowded room
choices.description: The household income is preserved, though the child suffers dull draughts and thin gruel.

choices.label: Scrape the jar so mother stays home at the hearth
choices.description: Tighten the belt and lose wages so mother can nurse and protect the infant.

storylets.title: The Dispensary Needle
storylets.text: A parish doctor visits the lane offering cowpox scratches against the smallpox plague. Neighbors murmur in distrust, but epidemics take many young souls each winter.

choices.label: Pay the dispensary fee and receive the protective scratch
choices.description: A sharp sting on the arm shields you from the dreaded pox.

choices.label: Rely on herbal washes and family prayer
choices.description: Keep the coins for bread; pray the winter chills pass over your door.

storylets.title: Mud and Iron Wheels
storylets.text: In the soot-choked alleys, older children run between heavy dray wagons and canal barges. You slip past the doorstep into the bustling street.

choices.label: Tumble through the mud with the street pack
choices.description: Run wild in the alleys; street wit and tough grit grow, though dray carts rumble close.

choices.label: Keep close to the threshold by the coal bucket
choices.description: Stay obediently near home, sheltered from horses and the chill drizzle.

storylets.title: The Worn Hornbook
storylets.text: A cousin leaves behind a wooden hornbook with printed letters shielded under transparent horn. You trace the dark symbols with charcoal fingers.

choices.label: Spend evenings sounding out letters and vowels
choices.description: Learn the marks of speech early; curiosity and literacy take deep root.

choices.label: Set the tablet aside and haul water and cinders
choices.description: Small hands carry small loads; you earn a few farthings helping the house.

storylets.title: Whispers After the Inquest
storylets.text: The Crown inspector's report ordered iron guardrails around the spinning frames. The mill owner is furious about the expenses, and the overseer corners you by the grease vats.

choices.label: Look the overseer in the eye and cite the Crown inspector
choices.description: Stand firm on the truth; union respect spreads among workers, though the masters mark you.

choices.label: Bow your head and promise unyielding toil
choices.description: Yield pride to keep the bread on the table; the overseer relents with an extra shift.

storylets.title: The Journeyman's Anvil
storylets.text: After years of hauling coal and tending the bellows, the master smith hands you the heavy cross-peen hammer to forge a steam-engine bracket without guidance.

choices.label: Strike the red-hot iron and shape the bracket
choices.description: A test of endurance and skill; success earns journeyman standing and skilled wages.

choices.label: Confess unreadiness and remain at the bellows
choices.description: Safe and modest; keep your apprentice spot without risking the master's scorn.

storylets.title: The Winter Shivers
storylets.text: Freezing rain turns the unpaved streets to icy slush. Scarlet fevers and chest rattles sweep through the cellar dwellings, taking the weakest first.

choices.label: Wrap in wool blankets by the chimney
choices.description: Endure the chills with home broth; saves coin but strains growing lungs.

choices.label: Buy quinine cordial from the apothecary
choices.description: Bitter bark medicine eases the burning fever and guards against relapse.

storylets.title: The Sobriety Dividend
storylets.text: Because you kept your signature on the temperance roll and stayed clear of the gin-shops, the parish society invites you to their annual jubilee.

choices.label: Accept the mutual relief dividend and gift of books
choices.description: The society rewards your steadfast character with financial support and books.

choices.label: Direct the relief fund to a poorer widow in the lane
choices.description: A display of quiet honor; your local reputation and moral stature rise.

storylets.title: Knocks of the Bailiff ({debt}s Debt)
storylets.text: Household arrears have mounted to {debt} shillings. A local bailiff hammers on the timber door with a distraint order. You must satisfy the ledger or brace for the debtor's court.

choices.label: Surrender the cast-iron stove and feather bolster to the cart
choices.description: The debt drops by 350s, but the hearth goes cold and sickness creeps in.

choices.label: Bar the door and face the magistrate's summons
choices.description: Refuse to strip the house bare; risk arrest or labor penalty if your spirit falters.

storylets.title: The Empty Flour Bin
storylets.text: The flour sack is scraped clean; {child} weeps with an empty belly. Behind the market, sweeping sweepings of bruised flour are sold cheap, while dark barges dock on the canal.

choices.label: Slip down to the canal barges in the fog to haul spilled grain
choices.description: Dangerous night toil feeds the home, though night watchmen brandish heavy clubs.

choices.label: Wait at the vestry steps for parish charity gruel
choices.description: Bitter to pride, but fills empty bowls without the peril of the canals.

storylets.title: Choked Air in the Cellar
storylets.text: {dwelling} has grown suffocating with too many souls under low rafters. {sibling} shivers in the damp corner, coughing up dark phlegm in the stifling cellar air.

choices.label: Scrape together private coins to rent an attic room
choices.description: Costly personal sacrifice clears the air and mends frail lungs.

choices.label: Huddle tight and endure the cellar dampness
choices.description: Coins stay in hand, but the pestilential air exacts its toll on body and spirit.

storylets.title: The Weight of Kin ({sibling})
storylets.text: {sibling} has collapsed with lung-rot from mill lint. The family expects you to abandon all personal ambitions and nurse them through the long months.

choices.label: Step back from work to nurse your sick sibling
choices.description: Noble sacrifice of your own station; family bonds and character deepen.

choices.label: Refuse to sacrifice your post; keep working for coin
choices.description: Hard-hearted but realistic; you bring home wages while leaving care to others.

storylets.title: The Turn-Out at the Mill
storylets.text: The mill hands have stopped the steam engines and called a turn-out over brutal 12-hour shifts. The overseer offers immediate promotion and double pay if you break the line, while your fellow spinners demand solidarity.

choices.label: Join the picket line and stand with the union
choices.description: Sacrifice wages and face constable batons, but uphold class honor and worker dignity.

choices.label: Slip past pickets and work for double wages
choices.description: Pocket gold and earn the master's gratitude, but face eternal curses from your neighbors.

storylets.title: The Molten Crucible Crisis
storylets.text: A crane chain snaps above the casting pit, sending white-hot iron pouring toward the engine moulds. The master calls for an experienced hand to throw the sand barriers before the foundry is destroyed.

choices.label: Hurl yourself into the smoke with the sand scoop
choices.description: A daredevil act of craftsmanship that could make you a legend or maim you for life.

choices.label: Fall back and let the metal spill
choices.description: Preserve your skin and breath; the moulds can be remade, but flesh cannot.

storylets.title: The Merchant's Secret Ledger
storylets.text: While balancing the shipping manifests, you uncover a double ledger hiding smuggled cotton bales from the customs taxman. The merchant summons you into his private office with a stack of banknotes on his mahogany desk.

choices.label: Take the clerk's share and sign the doctored ledger
choices.description: Secure an immediate promotion and cash bounty, binding your fate to a rogue master.

choices.label: Refuse to commit forgery and lay down your pen
choices.description: Preserve your Christian conscience and integrity, accepting immediate dismissal.

storylets.title: A Shop of One's Own
storylets.text: A corner grocer on Deansgate is retiring, offering the lease and dry goods stock for upfront capital. You have the savings to step out of the wage-earning herd and become your own master.

choices.label: Invest your hard-won savings and hoist your nameboard
choices.description: Leave the factory floor forever to become an independent shopkeeper.

choices.label: Hesitate and keep the safety of your bankroll
choices.description: Play it safe; keep working for wages while hoarding family coins.

storylets.title: The Tainted Broad Street Pump
storylets.text: A deadly blue cholera outbreak has struck the neighboring parish. The church bell tolls ceaselessly. Physicians warn that the street pump is poisoned with cesspool seep, urging all families to boil their kettle or buy carter-drawn spring water.

choices.label: Boil all household water and purchase clean carter supply
choices.description: Spend precious shillings on extra coal and water carters, shielding your kin from the blue death.

choices.label: Continue drawing free water from the alley pump
choices.description: Save coins for bread; pray that God spares your hearth from the deadly flux.

storylets.title: The Cotton Spinner's Phthisis
storylets.text: Years of inhaling airborne cotton lint have left your chest tight as an iron band. Every dawn begins with racking coughs and spit flecked with blood. An old weaver advises you to take the country air before your lungs rot away.

choices.label: Spend savings on a month in the Derbyshire hills
choices.description: Breathe pure moorland air and drink fresh goat milk; a costly refuge that restores your breath.

choices.label: Dull the pain with Godfrey's Cordial and keep working
choices.description: Rely on cheap opium syrup to suppress the cough; stay by your spindles while your health wanes.

storylets.title: The Surgeon's Saw and the Paved Flesh
storylets.text: A compound fracture from a factory accident has turned foul with black putrefaction. The parish infirmary surgeon rolls up his blood-crusted apron, brandishing his bone saw: 'It is the leg, lad, or the churchyard by Sunday.'

choices.label: Bite on the wooden peg and submit to the saw
choices.description: Survive the agony of the knife; you will walk on crutches, but your life is preserved.

choices.label: Push the surgeon away and trust home poultices
choices.description: Refuse to become a cripple; risk mortal fever in hopes that the wound cleanses itself.

storylets.title: The Manchester Exchange Club Blackball
storylets.text: Having accumulated significant savings, you submit an application to the prestigious Manchester Exchange Club. Yet the aristocratic committee whispers behind their port glasses, plotting to blackball you as a vulgar upstart from the mill alleys.

choices.label: Endow the club reading room with a grand donation
choices.description: Grease the committee's palms with heavy gold, purchasing polite acceptance among the gentry.

choices.label: Spurn the pretensions of the snobs with pride
choices.description: Walk away with your head high; your money was forged by honest sweat, not inherited privileges.

storylets.title: The Lancashire Brogue Dilemma
storylets.text: At a regional commercial assembly, your coarse Northern vowels draw quiet smirks from London merchants. An impoverished Oxford tutor offers evening elocution lessons to iron out your dialect and teach the Queen's English.

choices.label: Hire the tutor to master polite Southern diction
choices.description: Disguise your mill roots behind cultured speech, opening doors in mercantile drawing rooms.

choices.label: Refuse to parrot the South; speak straight Lancashire
choices.description: Keep your honest dialect; let your deeds and craftsmanship speak louder than polished vowels.

storylets.title: The Front Pew Auction
storylets.text: St. Ann's Church is auctioning annual leases for the cushioned box pews near the altar. Respectable tradesmen and mill owners sit there in broadcloth; sitting in the free benches at the back marks you as an indigent laborer.

choices.label: Bid for a front pew and secure a family brass plate
choices.description: Demonstrate your respectable station before God and the parish vestry.

choices.label: Sit in the free unheated benches with the laborers
choices.description: Reject the commercial vanity of the church; worship in humility without squandering coin.

storylets.title: The Fugitives of Little Ireland
storylets.text: An Irish weaver's family, fleeing the blight in Mayo, has arrived in the cellars of Little Ireland. Cold, soaked, and speaking only Gaelic, they huddle on the cobbles outside your door with a sick infant.

choices.label: Share half your loaf and offer an old wool blanket
choices.description: Costly charity from your own lean larder, but an act of Christian brotherhood that binds your hearts.

choices.label: Shut the latch and warn them away from your entry
choices.description: Preserve your own bread for your children; the town has too many hungry mouths already.

storylets.title: The Pioneer Co-operative Store
storylets.text: Fellow weavers are founding a mutual co-operative store on Toad Lane to sell pure, unadulterated flour and honest oatmeal without chalk dust or usurious shop debt. They invite you to purchase a member share.

choices.label: Subscribe twenty shillings for a member share in the store
choices.description: Secure pure bread, annual patronage dividends, and mutual independence from greedy middle-men.

choices.label: Keep buying on credit at the local tally-shop
choices.description: Hold onto hard silver today, tolerating watery milk and chalky bread on credit.

storylets.title: The Great Crystal Palace Excursion
storylets.text: The Year 1851 has arrived! London is marveling at Prince Albert's Crystal Palace of iron and glass. The railway company is running cheap excursion trains straight from Manchester to Hyde Park.

choices.label: Buy the excursion ticket and marvel at the Crystal Palace
choices.description: Journey by steam through the green shires to behold the crowning wonders of the industrial world.

choices.label: Save the shillings and stay by your daily toil
choices.description: A grand glass palace puts no butter on your bread; keep your head down and keep working.

storylets.title: The Monster Charter Petition
storylets.text: Thousands of working men gather by torchlight on Kersal Moor, demanding the People's Charter: universal manhood suffrage, vote by secret ballot, and an end to mill-owner parliaments. The petition parchment is passed to your hand.

choices.label: Dip the iron pen and sign your name boldly
choices.description: Join three million working Britons demanding justice, risking police watch and millmaster fury.

choices.label: Decline to sign and fade into the crowd
choices.description: Politics is rich men's game; stay clear of constables and sedition charges.
